subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer
skillName: Wave and Particle Models of Light

items.prompt:
The particles of light are called
A) photons
B) electrons
C) protons
D) atoms

Light bending and forming patterns is explained by the
A) wave model
B) particle model
C) heat model
D) sound model

steps: Wave behaviors need the wave model.

items.prompt:
The particle model describes light as
A) a stream of photons
B) a smooth wave only
C) a liquid
D) a solid

Scientists use two models for light because
A) each explains different behaviors of light
B) one model is wrong
C) light has no behaviors
D) they cannot decide
items.answer: A) each explains different behaviors of light

items.prompt:
Light knocking electrons off a metal is best explained by the
A) particle model
B) wave model
C) sound model
D) heat model

steps: Photons knocking off electrons fit the particle model.

items.prompt:
A photon is
A) a packet of light energy
B) a sound wave
C) a type of metal
D) a water drop
items.answer: A) a packet of light energy

items.prompt:
Evaluate: 'Light is only a wave.' This is
A) incomplete, because light also shows particle behavior, so it is both
B) completely true
C) proof light has no wave behavior
D) about sound
items.answer: A) incomplete, because light also shows particle behavior, so it is both

items.prompt:
Light is described as both a wave and particles because
A) it behaves like a wave in some situations and like particles in others
B) it is neither
C) it is only a particle
D) models do not matter
items.answer: A) it behaves like a wave in some situations and like particles in others
